newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany mulling petrol tax rise from July - paper.
newsitem.headline: Germany mulling petrol tax rise from July - paper.

text.p: Germany is considering raising petrol tax by 18 pfennigs per litre from July 1 this year, Bild-Zeitung newspaper reported on Monday.
The resulting increase in tax revenues by 15 billion marks would be used to reduce unemployment benefit contributions by one percentage point, the paper said.
Bild said the reduction in jobless benefit contributions would be a possible concession by the government to the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) in a protracted dispute over plans for a tax reform.
The SPD has demanded a reduction in non-wage labour costs as a precondition for agreeing to the tax reform plan, the paper said.
Under the reform plan, the government intends to cut 30 billion marks in income and corporate taxes to increase investment and reduce joblessness which was running at 11.2 percent in March.
But the SPD can block most tax measures through its control of the upper house of parliament.

The ruling coalition of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), the CDU's Bavarian sister party CSU and the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) is scheduled to meet the SPD on Wednesday for more discussions on the tax reform after little progress was made in talks last Tuesday.
The tax reform's timing is critical as the government tries to trim its budget deficit to meet the strict entry criteria for European monetary union.
